quote: A concept analysis according to the Walker and Avant (2011) framework was used, to investigate the basic elements of the concept.
Through concept analysis and Delphi survey, five defining attributes for perinatal resilience were identified: social support, self-efficacy, self-esteem, sense of mastery and personality.

quote: Yet a definition of perinatal resilience is absent.

Resilience is generally understood as the ability to cope with the challenges, stresses, and adversities in life ( Waugh and Koster, 2015 ).

Following our analysis of the results, we propose a description of perinatal resilience for the first 1,000 days of life as follows: perinatal resilience is a circular process toward a greater well-being in the form of personal growth, family balance, adaptation, or acceptance, when faced with stressors, challenges, or adversity during the perinatal period.
Self-efficacy is described as the belief in one’s capability to achieve a goal or overcome an event ( Bandura, 1982 ; Earvolino-Ramirez, 2007 ).
Sense of mastery is defined as finding strength and meaningfulness following a stressful experience, adversity or trauma ( Elmir, 2014 ).
Self-esteem can be paraphrased as a positive or negative perspective toward oneself ( Hajek and König, 2019 ).
Optimism can be defined as the generalized expectancy that good outcomes will occur when confronting major problems ( Handelzalts et al., 2016 ).
The first 1,000 days of life refer to the period from conception to the age of the child up to 2 years.
A model case is an example of the use of the concept that demonstrates all the defining attributes of the concept ( Walker and Avant, 2011 ).
